verdict.rationale: Capacities documents custom object types with core properties, templates that prefill properties, AI auto-fill of properties, and AI tagging that reuses your existing tags. Community users corroborate the typed notes and tags, and graphs can be opened on a tag or query. However, the evidence never details the available property data types or how to filter and retrieve notes by property or tag values. missing for 10: documentation of typed property kinds (e.g., select, number, date) and how they are enforced, explicit property/tag-based filtering or query retrieval docs, hands-on corroboration of consistent use at scale.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can attach typed properties and tags to notes and use them consistently for organization and retrieval

citations.quote: Capacities is object-type-first. Define key object types early (`People`, `Projects`, `Meetings`, etc.) and add core properties.
Templates allow you to prefill the content of an object- you can prefill properties and blocks in your objects.
AI identifies relevant tags from your existing tags and assigns them to that object.
You can also open a graph on a collection, a tag, a query, an object type dashboard, or in extended search.
Rather than manually filling in the properties of your custom objects, you can rely on the AI model's knowledge to auto-fill them for you.
